segments.narration: A cargo of over 1,700 barrels of pure alcohol remained entirely intact in the hold. In December 1872, the brigantine Mary Celeste was discovered adrift and deserted in the Atlantic Ocean off the Azores.
Sailors from the Canadian brigantine Dei Gratia boarded the vessel, finding the cabin interior wet and untidy, with personal items scattered about.
Yet not a single crew member remained. Even stranger, the ship's primary navigation instruments and only lifeboat were entirely gone.
Decades of wild theories blamed giant squids and sea monsters. But modern historians point to a much simpler, terrifying panic aboard.

Captain Briggs smelled leaking fumes from the cargo casks and feared an imminent explosion. The crew abandoned ship into a lifeboat that was later swamped by rough seas. Was it a rational fear that sealed their fate?
